doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Where his original compositions come from
summary: He gets ideas from bass lines, voice memos, lyrics, and Ellington and Monk, including a calypso version of Let's Cool One.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Where do you get inspiration from for your original compositions?

A lot of different places. Other people’s tunes, something I hear somebody say in the street sometimes or bird calls. Sometimes I’m just sitting at the piano and I come up with a bass line that’s kind of cool and I say this could be something. So I make a voice memo of it. And maybe nothing happens but maybe a week later I listen to it and I say yeah, that was a cool idea, how about this? I’ll add a couple of chords here and sometimes a tune is built that way. Sometimes I write lyrics. Don’t ask me to sing them but I write them and sometimes they will inspire the whole tune. I’m singing the lyrics to myself or that becomes the melody but then the tune is sort of written around that form. You know here’s two verses, a chorus and a bridge and another verse and two choruses. So that kind of denotes the form of the tune and gives me a melody and a bridge. It’s always something different. There’s a lot of composers that I really admire, you know Duke Ellington and Monk especially. And I’m often inspired by one of their tunes. Or like on this new album “Let’s Cool One” is one of my favorite Monk tunes so I did like a calypso version of it. Cool-ypso.
